About

Estimating built on craft, not volume

Qostara is a construction cost estimating firm that grew from a two-person desk in San Francisco into a distributed team serving general contractors, specialty trades, and owners across the United States.

Work with usOur services

Our story

From a Bay Area desk to a national estimating practice

Amelia Rowe founded Qostara in 2008 after a decade as a chief estimator at a mid-market general contractor. She saw smaller firms competing against nationals with a fraction of the preconstruction depth — and built Qostara to close that gap.

Today we are a team of twenty-five-plus estimators, quantity surveyors, and client success leads. We take fewer jobs than the big outsourcing shops so every takeoff survives a peer review and a superintendent's scrutiny on site.

Whether you are bidding a tilt-up warehouse or pricing a design-build healthcare pursuit, you get a named estimator who knows your standards — not a rotating queue.

Purpose

What drives every takeoff we deliver

Two commitments that shape how we scope work, staff accounts, and review deliverables before they leave the desk.

Mission

Give every contractor bid-ready numbers they can defend

We turn drawings into precise quantity takeoffs and cost models — CSI-formatted, source-referenced, and reviewed by a second estimator before delivery. Accuracy is the product, not a marketing line.

Vision

Preconstruction depth for the mid-market

We believe growing contractors and specialty trades deserve the same estimating rigour as the nationals — without the overhead of a full in-house department or the opacity of a black-box outsourcing shop.

Values

How we work when the bid date is close

These principles show up in every scope review, every peer check, and every conversation with your team.

  • Precision over volume

    We take fewer jobs so every takeoff can survive a peer review. Accuracy is the product.

  • Clarity in every deliverable

    If a superintendent cannot find the source of a quantity, the estimate is not finished.

  • Partnership, not a black box

    You always know who is working the set and how the numbers were built.

  • Craft with modern tools

    Digitised takeoff platforms, live cost libraries — applied by people who have swung hammers.
